Principles of Computer Science I. Prerequisite: Only for STEM majors and minors. Co-requisite: CSC 1301L. Students must be enrolled in MATH 1111 or 1113 (or a higher level mathematics course excluding MATH 1401) or have previously completed one of these courses with a C or higher. This course is an introduction to the fundamental principles of programming and data analysis in computer science. It emphasizes structured, top-down development and testing of computer programs. The course includes an overview of computers and programming; problem solving and algorithm development; basic data types; arithmetic and logic operators; selection structures; repetition structures; text files; arrays; procedural abstraction and software design. This course may be taken a maximum of two times.
